newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Aug 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Aug 12.

text.p: THE AUSTRALIAN

After another failure in Hong Kong, Australian cricket captain Mark Taylor has been given the first two tests in the up-coming Ashes series to improve his form, otherwise, according to coach Geoff Marsh, he will be replaced by vice-captain Steve Waugh. Mrsh's announcement comes after an admission by Taylor on Saturday he will drop himself if his form does not improve. Page 19

Following a disappointing start to the Australian Football League season, North Melbourne coach Denis Pagan is still to agree to terms with the club for a new contract. Pagan is understood to be seeking a four-year deal worth around A$1 million, but Nort officials are reported to want to pay Pagan around A$25,000 a season less. Page 19.

Adelaide Crows coach Malcolm Blight has described his team's last quarter performance yesterday against premiership favourites Essendon as the best he has seen. The Crows won at Football Park by 53 points, after only one point separated the two teams goig into the final quarter. Page 19.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Manly coach Bob Fulton has diverted attention away from his team's 26-all-draw with Australian Rugby League struggler Gold Coast yesterday, by criticising New South Wales Premier Bob Carr, Olympics Minister Michael Knight and State Treasurer Michael Egan for not consulting with clubs over an increase to the surcharge on the profits of licensed clubs. Page 27.

Australian tennis player Jason Stoltenburg will defend his title at America's red clay championship after a convincing win in the semi-final against Jonas Van Herck of Belgium. Fourth seed Stoltenburg will now meet Swede Jonas Borgman in the final of thechampionship. Page 27.

Next week's game between the ACT Brumbies and the Wellington Hurricanes, currently second and third on the table, will decide whether the semi-final the following week is held in Australia or New Zealand. Page 28.
THE AGE

Struggling Australian Football team the Melbourne Demons was dealt a cruel blow on Saturday night when its star forward David Neitz suffered a broken jaw after a collision with Fremantle's Craig Callaghan. Team doctors are now predicting Neitz could missthe rest of the season after he undergoes surgery this week. Page Sports3.

The Brisbane Lions have continued their poor form, losing to the West Coast Eagles at the Gabba yesterday. It was the team's worst performance on the ground since moving there in 1993, which led to coach John Northey refusing to address his players afterthe match. Page Sports3.

World number one golfer Greg Norman has failed to capitalise on a strong start and fell five strokes behind the leaders in the BellSouth Atlanta Classic in the United States yesterday. Norman, who became visibly annoyed towards the end of the round, shota one-over-par 73 to slip to ninth position. Page 16.
THE HERALD SUN

The Carlton Football Club will begin a week of off-field activities today, starting with negotiations with Anthony Koutoufides over the brand of boots the player will wear in this season's competition. Tomorrow, veteran Greg Williams will confront the Sureme Court to appeal a nine-week suspension for pushing an umpire, whilst captain Stephen Kernahan awaits possible action after an alleged striking incident with Richmond player Duncan Kellaway. Page 88.

The Melbourne Phoenix netball team will today appeal to the sport's officials to sort out a colour clash which occurred in their match against the Adelaide Thunderbirds on Saturday night. Phoenix players say they had difficulty in pin-pointing their teammates in the game, which they eventually won 53-47. Page 84.

The South Melbourne soccer team has booked a preliminary final place against Sydney United next week after a dramatic win against Adelaide City last night. With both teams locked at nil-all after regulation time, South player Bill Damianos scored with 45seconds remaining of extra time. Page 82.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

For the first time since 1989, the Australian Rugby League was yesterday forced to abandon a match due to played between the Knights and South Sydney at Newcastle's Marathon Stadium, because of atrocious weather conditions and the state of the ground. Th cancellation means Newcastle stars Andrew and Matthew Johns will only have one game next week to force their way into the New South Wales squad for the State of Origin match against Queensland. Page 34

Australian netball coach Jill McIntosh believes South Africa is hiding some of its talent from the Australian team in the lead up to the 1998 Commonwealth Games. McIntosh's announcement came after she received news of the South African team for the up-coing Test series against Australia, which contains a host of young and inexperienced players. Page 42.

Australian distance swimmer Susie Maroney has announced she will make an attempt on the Cuba to America swim this week, regardless of the weather conditions which have plagued her attempt over the past week. Maroney's mother Pauline says the delays are sarting to have a negative affect on Susie, and so the team will leave Havana in the next few days. Page 42.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
